_comment: #892 Phase 3 — the inverse of ci.yml's `changes` filter table. `skipped` counts as a PASS in the required `check` job, which makes that table load-bearing: a path no filter names wakes no path-gated lane and merges green, unexercised (#890 W0 fixed one instance of exactly this by hand). scripts/lint-path-filters.mjs requires every workspace package, every app and every tracked top-level directory to be claimed by a filter OR to appear here with the ALWAYS-ON job that covers it. An entry naming a path that no longer exists fails as stale — a dead exemption reads like a reviewed decision and is not one.

alwaysOn.assets: Product icon sources (13 files: the .svg masters plus the generated .icns/.ico/.png). They are consumed at PACKAGING time by lane-release-desktop.yml and lane-release-mobile.yml, not by any PR lane — there is no per-PR claim about them to gate, and the release lanes rebuild from them unconditionally on every tag.
alwaysOn.packages/test-kit: Test-only harness (no product surface, not shipped in any artifact). It is covered by `verify`, which is unfiltered and runs the whole vitest suite — the only consumer that matters. It is deliberately NOT in the client/gateway filters: the Playwright e2e lanes do not import it, so waking them on a test-kit change would cost minutes and prove nothing.
alwaysOn.contracts: The v1 tree's language-neutral fixtures and ledgers (#1020). Covered by gate.yml — `cargo xtask gate --profile pr` on every PR, UNFILTERED, by ruling: the v1 gate is one command with one step list and no `paths:` table at all, so there is no lane to wake selectively and nothing for ci.yml's filter table to claim.
alwaysOn.crates: The v1 Rust workspace (#1020). Covered by gate.yml — `cargo xtask gate --profile pr` on every PR, UNFILTERED, for the same reason as `contracts` above: `cargo fmt/clippy/test --workspace` and the structural rules see the whole tree on every run, and the nightly profile adds the v0 oracle on top of it.
alwaysOn.receipts: The audit trail itself. Covered by `governance.yml` (unfiltered, runs .governance/run.sh on every PR) which owns receipt-per-issue, commit-issue-receipt-match and doc-integrity, plus `gates`' check:ui-receipt. A receipt change has no product lane to wake.
alwaysOn.desktop: The v1 desktop seat (#1020 wave 3 lane F): Electron main, the renderer, and the Playwright run. Covered by gate.yml — `cargo xtask gate --profile pr` runs `desktop-unit` (the vitest project over desktop/ and extension/, plus the three tsconfigs) on every PR, UNFILTERED, for the same reason as `crates` and `contracts` above: the v1 gate is one command with one step list and no `paths:` table, so there is no lane to wake selectively. The `desktop-e2e` step — a real Electron app over a real sidecar, which is the lane's exit criterion — is in the nightly profile because it builds a binary and launches a browser; see contracts/handoff/F/desktop-e2e.md for why that split is where it is.
alwaysOn.extension: The v1 browser Companion (#1020 wave 3 lane F): MV3 over native messaging, no network and no WASM. Its pure layer is in the SAME vitest project as desktop/ — one more consumer of the same seat socket — so `desktop-unit` in gate.yml's `pr` profile covers it on every PR, UNFILTERED. It is deliberately not in any ci.yml filter: nothing in the v0 tree imports it, so waking a v0 lane on an extension change would cost minutes and prove nothing.
